title: DocReport
description: Canonical shape of tasks/<task-id>/iterations/<NNN>/doc-report.json — the machine-readable companion to selection-doc.md. It carries the provenance the document body deliberately omits (see agents/documentation-generator.md § 'Provenance without leakage'), the requirement index the Reviewer cites, and this iteration's responses to routed findings. Validated structurally by scripts/validate_artifacts.py.

document.description: Path to the selection document this report accompanies, relative to the iteration directory (normally 'selection-doc.md').

sources.description: The numbered source table. Ids are cited from selection-doc.md by id alone; this is the only place the underlying paths appear.

source_id.description: S* = external/reference source, C* = in-repository code or config, P* = POG/official entry point.

location.description: File path with optional line range, config key, URL, or document citation.

requirements.description: Index of every requirement stated in selection-doc.md. Ids are stable across iterations and never reused.

section.description: The selection-doc.md section it lives in, e.g. 'muons', 'trigger', 'event-selection'.

enforcement.description: Whether the framework actually applies this requirement, merely computes/flags it, only stores the input, or does not implement it at all. See agents/documentation-generator.md § 'Rules'.

era_scope.description: Eras the requirement applies to; omit or leave empty when it applies to all.

open_questions.description: What could not be established from the source, phrased so a physicist could answer it.

responses.description: How this iteration answered each finding routed to the Documentation Generator.

misrouted_findings.description: Findings routed here that are not documentation defects — the document was correct and the defect lies downstream. The Reviewer re-routes these to the Code Generator; they are never absorbed by editing the document to compensate.

correct_requirements.description: The requirement ids that were already stated correctly, evidencing that the document is not at fault.
